entry.dc:title: STUDYING THE PRODUCTION SYSTEM OF SURFACE MINES BY USING A COMPUTER SIMULATION METHOD.
entry.dc:creator: Wang S.
entry.dc:description: A description is given of fundamental concepts, steps to be followed, simulation methods, and random variables. Finally, an example is given of the simple loading, drainage, and transportation systems of a surface mine.

entry.dc:title: SAMPLERS PINPOINT SURFACE DUST.
entry.dc:creator: Heimbach J.A.
entry.dc:description: This article tells how to set up an air-quality network around a surface mine to monitor suspended particulates. Included are highlights of federal and state regulations.

entry.dc:title: IMPACT OF PUBLIC POLICY ON SURFACE MINE PLANNING AND DESIGN IN THE UNITED STATES.
entry.dc:creator: Sweigard R.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
entry.dc:description: The major effects that public policy has had on the planning design, and organization of surface mines in the United States are summarized in this paper. The public policy impacts are grouped into three separate categories: mine planning, mine design, and mine organization. A clear distinction is made between the Federal, state, and local governmental responsibilities in formulating public policy with regard to surface mining operations.

entry.dc:title: SURFACE MINING - PAST, PRESENT AND FUTURE.
entry.dc:creator: Atkinson T.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
entry.dc:description: The article reviews the history, current state-of-the-art and future trends of development in the field of surface mining. The main topics discussed cover the limits of scale of surface mining operations performed by walking draglines and bucket wheel excavators; mine design and planning for strip, terrace and open-pit mining; ground preparation including drilling and blasting operations; loading and haulage equipment; and surface mine electric power systems.

entry.dc:title: SURFACE MINE ELECTRICAL POWER SYSTEM DESIGN.
entry.dc:creator: Atkinson T.
entry.prism:publicationName: Transactions of the Institution of Mining and Metallurgy Section A Mining Technology
entry.dc:description: The steps in surface mine electric power system design are discussed in logical order for strip mines, terrace mines and open-pits, attention being paid to voltage regulation, fault-level calculations, earthing systems, transient voltage problems and system layout. The problems of production losses and their prevention, diversity calculations and weak power systems are highlighted.

entry.dc:title: CONTINUOUS SURFACE MINE MATERIALS HANDLING SYSTEMS.
entry.dc:creator: Brady T.M.
entry.dc:description: This paper presents a review of three ongoing research projects dealing with continuous materials handling systems in open-pit mines in the USA. The systems include mine-run-rock conveyors, high-angle conveyors, and movable in-pit crushers. These material handling systems are being evaluated and applied to mining systems primarily to reduce the dependency on diesel fuel and to reduce mining costs.

entry.dc:title: WHAT CAUSED SURFACE MINE PRODUCTIVITY TO DECLINE - A CASE STUDY.
entry.dc:creator: Herhal A.
entry.dc:description: Surface coal mine productivity in the Illinois basin peaked in 1967 at about 45 tons per man-day (manshift). Since then, surface mine output has exhibited a drop to less than 20 tons per man-day. The article is a case study of a large midwestern, union surface mine.

entry.dc:title: GAMMS RAYS, LASER AID SURFACE MINE.
entry.dc:creator: Jackson D.
entry.dc:description: A Wyoming mine uses a hand-held gamma ray scintillometer to help loader operators detect a parting. A laser guides coal haulers through a narrow crossover dump.

entry.dc:title: Coal surface mine land reclamation costs ( USA).
entry.dc:creator: Misiolek W.S.
entry.dc:description: In the light of a lack of consistency in prior reclamation cost estimates and apparent methodological problems, attempts to develop an economic method for estimating costs of land reclamation for large-scale ore mining operations in the USA. The mine simulation approach is extended to include relevant opportunity costs. The cost impacts of federal reclamation regulations in different regions are also compared.-K.Turner

entry.dc:title: Characteristics of bird communities on surface mine lands in Pennsylvania
entry.dc:creator: Brenner F.
entry.dc:description: A variety of species was observed as either visitors, permanent, or summer residents on surface mines with different ecological adaptations. Passerine species were the most prevalent of the 25 families represented. Bird communities as well as individual species were correlated with the structure and species of vegetation on the mines. The composition of the bird communities changed in response to successional vegetation stages from grassland to forest communities. © 1981 Springer-Verlag New York Inc.

entry.dc:title: The impact of surface mine reclamation on headwater streams in Southwest Virginia
entry.dc:creator: Matter W.J.
entry.dc:description: Recovery of headwater streams following the cessation of mining and the application of terrestrial (vegetative) reclamation techniques was assessed by comparison of water quality and aquatic biota in two such systems (reclaimed four to seven years) with that of an unimpacted stream and of streams draining mine areas which were abandoned without reclamation. Alkalinity, hardness, sulfate, and conductivity were elevated in the reclaimed mine streams as were fine-particle suspended solids and sediment. Overall water quality was comparable to streams draining unreclaimed lands. Benthic invertebrate and fish populations were significantly lower in abundance in the reclaimed mine streams than in the reference stream and showed less taxonomic richness and stability; they were similar in these respects to the biota of the unreclaimed mine streams. Continued sedimentation from mined areas and haul roads affected stream habitat and appeared to be the major factor limiting biotic recovery. These findings emphasize that terrestrial reclamation does not assure lotic restoration. Water quality criteria merit consideration in the refinement of reclamation procedures for mined lands. © 1981 Dr. W. Junk B.V. Publishers.

entry.dc:title: Evaluation of hydraulic coal transport system concepts for surface mines.
entry.dc:creator: Roberge J.
entry.dc:description: The objective of the programme was to develop concepts for in-pit hydraulic transport systems for surface coal mines that will permit significant increases in coal extraction and pit haulage productivity as compared to truck haulage. Large particle coal transport was demonstrated to be the most desirable for central and western United States surface mines. Three conceptual hydrotransport systems, including a centrifugal pump, jet pump and ventilated inducer system, were developed for each of two currently active mining operations. General and site specific design parameters were developed for each of the conceptual hydrotransport systems. A detailed economic comparison of capital and operating and maintenance costs for each of the hydrotransport systems was made with the existing truck haul operations. An increase in haulage productivity of approximately 19% was demonstrated for the central surface mine, while that of the western surface mine increased by more than 180%. Included in this report is a bibliography containing over 600 citations pertinent to hydraulic transport of coal. (from authors' abstract)

entry.dc:title: Testing of a cornering water-jet-drilling system for drilling horizontal holes in coal.
entry.dc:creator: Love S.
entry.dc:description: A drilling system which uses high pressure water jets to drill horizontal holes in a coal seam is presented. The drilling head, an articulated drill string, and an instrumentation system for directional control and hole mapping of the water jet drill have been developed and tested. In recent tests, six to eight inch diameter holes of up to 102 feet long were drilled into a coal seam accessed at the face of a surface mine pit. A quarter scale laboratory model of the cornering device was built and tested to evaluate the design, and hardware is being built for the full scale version.

entry.dc:title: AIRBLAST INSTRUMENTAION AND MEASUREMENT TECHNIQUES FOR SURFACE MINE BLASTING.
entry.dc:creator: Stachura V.
entry.prism:publicationName: Report of Investigations United States Bureau of Mines
entry.dc:description: Results include equivalencies between broadband research instrumentation and commercially available impulse precision sound level meters measuring: root-mean-square, peak, fast, slow, impulse, A and C weighting, C-weighted sound exposure level (CSEL), and ″linear″ (flat) response. These values were obtained from field measurements and broadband FM tape recordings of production blasts at area and contour coal mines, limestones quarries, and iron mines. Frequency response was determined for 14 commercial systems.

entry.dc:title: Lead-210 analyses of sediment accumulation rates in five southern Illinois surface mine lakes.
entry.dc:creator: Brugam R.
entry.prism:publicationName: Proc 1981 Symposium on Surface Mining Hydrology Sedimentology and Reclamation University of Kentucky Lexington College of Engineering
entry.dc:description: 210Pb is a naturally occurring radionuclide with a short half-life (22 yrs) which can be used to determine sedimentation rates in lakes. entry.dc:title: Establishing European alder seedlings in fescue covered surface mine spoil.
entry.dc:creator: Carpenter S.B.
entry.dc:description: Alnus glutinosa seedlings were planted in an established ground cover of Kentucky-31 fescue Festuca arundinacea of surface mine spoil in SE Kentucky. Highest survival (43%) occurred in plots where competing vegetation was mechanically scalped away from seedlings. Scalping increased the soil moisture available for growth and reduced water stress of seedlings.-from Authors

entry.dc:creator: Smith R.E.
entry.prism:publicationName: Transactions American Society of Agricultural Engineers
entry.dc:description: A general watershed runoff and sediment transport model is described that may be used in designing, analysing and managing small urban as well as agricultural watersheds. It is an extension of a model first developed by Rovey, et al. entry.dc:title: The Use of Geologic, Hydrologic, and Geochemical Mapping Techniques in Environmental Assessment
entry.dc:creator: Coe C.J.
entry.dc:description: A method of researching data at a mine to determine the environmental and economic impact to the operator has been developed. This method consists of developing geologic, hydrologic, and geochemical maps that can be used to provide a three‐dimensional view of the subsurface environment before, during, and after mining. The following maps were developed: a standard topographic base map, structure contour maps, static water level maps, and several iso‐concentration maps for pH, iron, manganese, sulfate, and specific conductance. Where possible geologic‐hydrologic cross sections were drawn to aid in the environmental interpretations. It is possible to use the data to develop the best possible mining plan for a geologic region which considers geographic, technical, economic, and environmental parameters. The iso‐concentration maps for a proposed surface mine site can be used to define the extent of concentration fields, point source locations, and concentration gradients. To demonstrate the use and interpretations of the data provided by this method, the results of two mine site case studies are presented that will discuss: (1) Dewatering problems; (2) Mining recharge areas; (3) Mining coal overlain by an acid overburden; and (4) The impact of prior surface mining. entry.dc:title: Environmental control at a surface mine
entry.dc:creator: Hammond R.
entry.dc:description: The Woodlawn copper-lead-zinc-silver mine is situated 80 km from Canberra. Woodlawn Mine was the first new mine to come into operation in New South Wales during the surge of interest in environmental protection, and its experiences are a background for new mines now coming into operation elsewhere in the state.
